report_notes:
Package C ran three of its five review lenses: code, ragdoll feel and grab feel. The hit-feel and performance lenses were skipped for usage. Coverage against the plan:

**Code: complete.**
- Every edge case on the plan's list was checked except the player's own KO while holding.
- The list's "lock-on aimed at a blinking body" maps to magnetism. SPEC has no hard lock-on (SPEC: "Target magnetism (no hard lock-on)"), and no lock-on code exists. The reviewer probed magnetism on a blink-in dummy (code-04).
- A grab on a KO'd body that is blinking off is refused by `CombatActor.can_be_grabbed()`, which excludes `is_ko()` (`combat_actor.gd:251-265`). So "grab aimed at a blinking body" holds, although the reviewer only stated it for the blink-in.
- All six code findings are verified.

**Ragdoll: complete for the bot.**
- All 24 ragdoll_bot acts were judged in both views, and all five findings are verified.
- The flash on ragdolls was judged only in first person.
- The A/B of the contact push covered only the hook.

**Grab: complete for the bot's grab acts and the vfx_bot knees.**
- "Grab anytime" was only skimmed.
- grab-06, grab-07 and grab-08 are still unverified.

**Not reviewed by anyone:**
- 25 of combo_bot's 34 acts and 21 of vfx_bot's 22 acts, including every heavy-tier knockdown from the player's own moves and every act where the player gets hit.
- All seven known items from HANDOFF 10:55. Two were glimpsed, but neither got a verdict.
- Every performance question.

**What I checked myself (read-only):**
- **Speed lines:** VfxDirector randomizes its rng at `_init` (`game/fx/vfx_director.gd:76`), and only vfx_bot reseeds it (`tests/bot/vfx_bot.gd:73`). combo_bot and ragdoll_bot don't, so their captures still vary between runs. `game/fx/speed_lines.gd:26-27` ("the bots do") overstates it.
- **Block flash constant:** `BLOCK_FLASH_AMOUNT` (0.45, `combat_actor.gd:56`) dates from M1's held block (`bf3194f`), so it is not a new number in a script.
- **Flash warm-up:** the warm-up cites 4-12 ms on the first hit without it (`humanoid_rig.gd:454-457`). Whether it works is the open perf question.

**Ready to use:**
- The worktrees `/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-hit` and `/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-perf` exist, detached at c27afaf, imported, with empty `captures/`. The gap reviewer can start in m2-review-hit with no setup.
- WP4's frame-time probe can be reused: `/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-ragdoll/captures/review_mech/probe_perf.gd` (six dummies, headless physics wall time). Rendering costs need a windowed run.

**For the final report:**
- **Contact push:** the claim "the contact push looks the same as the central kick" rests on the hook alone in C. For Game-boy's open contortion question, cite A's five-move sheets in `.worktrees/m2-ragdoll2/captures/ab_contact/`.
- **Joint limits:** WP4's joint-limit transients were not re-measured with the contact twist on.
- **Tuning panel:** the F1 panel's new subgroups were never opened or changed live.

If usage allows only part of the gap round, run hit feel's known items (a), (b), (d), (e) and (f) and perf's first-hit and first-finisher measurements first. Those are the items Game-boy is most likely to notice in his first minute of play.
